info.title: Poster Judging API
info.description:
CRUD over every poster-judging resource.

**Authentication.** Admin endpoints use the Supabase session cookie; the single judge endpoint pair uses the `pj_judge` cookie. There are no bearer tokens yet — the API is same-origin only, and every mutating request must carry `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` (or an `Origin` matching the host) or it is refused with 403. Server Actions get that check from Next automatically; Route Handlers do not, so it is enforced explicitly.

**Cross-tenant access returns 404, never 403.** A 403 would confirm that a resource exists, letting a caller probe for other organisers' event and poster ids. "No such row" and "not yours" are deliberately indistinguishable.

**Unjudged is not zero.** A poster nobody has scored comes back with a null `raw_pct` and `norm_z` and is unranked. Do not coerce those nulls to 0.

put.description: PUT rather than POST because the operation already deletes every assignment and inserts a freshly dealt plan — that is a collection replacement, and it makes the call idempotent. Judges are dealt contiguous blocks of the walking order so each route stays physically walkable. Submissions are untouched: a judge who already scored a poster keeps that score even if the reshuffle moves it off their list.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: raw is the plain weighted average — the number to show presenters. normalized expresses each score as how far above or below that judge's own average it sits, which matters because no two posters are seen by the same set of judges.

put.summary: Save or submit one score sheet
put.description: PUT is exact, not approximate: the write upserts on (judge, poster) and replaces the child score rows wholesale, so replaying the same body leaves the same state. That is what makes the offline outbox safe to retry. A judge may score any poster in their own event, not only assigned ones. 409 means judging is closed — clients surface that inline and must never queue it.
